verifier.note: 2nd-stage verifier (vhead.* in wake.bin); thresholds measured on round-4 training windows. Dormant until car-tested: set enabled:true after confirming the 'verifier' score in the Kit log clears a real wake. At the measured gates it rejects 94/61/36% of the primary's false-positive windows (recall cost ~5/2/1%).

measured: ROUND 4 head (retrained 2026-11-19, 15.5 h held-out). The WEIGHTS are new; the GATE is deliberately kept at round 2's car-proven patience 3 / normal 0.95, NOT the auto-tuner's patience 4 / 0.99 — patience 4 + a high threshold is the exact config that went deaf on the car on 2026-11-02 (near miss 0.998 needs 0.950, one dip reset the run, owner needed 2 tries) and was rolled back. Round 4 is far cleaner on false wakes than round 2: 0.00 false wakes/h across 15.5 h even at threshold 0.9999 (round 2 was 0.19/h at normal), so 0.95 is safe. Held-out recall at the model's own saturated scores: greet 100%, road 5 dB 0.982, cabin 5 dB ~0.74, សួស្តី Avatar 100%; look-alikes at Normal mostly rejected (the_Avatar_car 60%, I_have_a_tire 48% are the leaks the dormant verifier targets). Java WakeEngine vs stream.py ONNX parity: max|Δprimary|=0, max|Δverifier|=2e-7 (both heads). Car test owed: (1) wakes reliably at patience 3/0.95, no round-3-style deafness; (2) then enable the verifier and confirm it cuts the leaky look-alikes without killing real wakes.
